This notebook gathers about 1,500 unique movies from the TMDb public REST
API and saves them to `data/movies_raw.csv`. Run this once before
`analysis.qmd`. Re-running it overwrites the CSV.

The default `TMDB_API_KEY` below is the one from my midterm. To use a
different key, set the `TMDB_API_KEY` environment variable in your
shell before running:

``` bash
export TMDB_API_KEY=your_key_here
quarto render collect_data.qmd
```

The notebook is set to `eval: false` so a render of the project does not
re-hit the API. Set `eval: true` (or run the cells interactively) to
actually collect the data.

## Setup

```{python}
#| label: setup
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
import json
from pathlib import Path

import requests
import pandas as pd

API_KEY = os.environ.get("TMDB_API_KEY", "939ed19c3d5487d60bf45c0c8e353499")
BASE_URL = "https://api.themoviedb.org/3"
TARGET_UNIQUE_MOVIES = 1500
SLEEP_SEC = 0.20
TIMEOUT = 30
PAGES_PER_STRATEGY = 30

DATA_DIR = Path.cwd() / "data"
DATA_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

## Sampling strategies

The midterm used `/movie/popular`, which returned the same trending
titles on every call and produced only 148 usable rows. For the final I
switched to `/discover/movie` and combined five sort strategies to widen
the sample.

```{python}
#| label: strategies
STRATEGIES = [
    ("popular_recent",
     {"sort_by": "popularity.desc", "vote_count.gte": 50,
      "primary_release_date.gte": "2015-01-01"}),
    ("popular_classic",
     {"sort_by": "popularity.desc", "vote_count.gte": 200,
      "primary_release_date.lte": "2014-12-31"}),
    ("most_voted",
     {"sort_by": "vote_count.desc", "vote_count.gte": 500}),
    ("top_rated",
     {"sort_by": "vote_average.desc", "vote_count.gte": 1000}),
    ("revenue_top",
     {"sort_by": "revenue.desc", "vote_count.gte": 100}),
]
```

## Collect movie IDs

```{python}
#| label: fetch-ids
def fetch_movie_ids():
    seen = set()
    ids = []
    for label, base_params in STRATEGIES:
        print(f"\n[{label}]")
        for page in range(1, PAGES_PER_STRATEGY + 1):
            params = {"api_key": API_KEY, "page": page, "language": "en-US",
                      "include_adult": "false"}
            params.update(base_params)
            try:
                r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/discover/movie",
                                 params=params, timeout=TIMEOUT)
                if r.status_code != 200:
                    print(f"  page {page}: HTTP {r.status_code}")
                    break
                results = r.json().get("results", [])
                if not results:
                    break
                for m in results:
                    mid = m.get("id")
                    if mid and mid not in seen:
                        seen.add(mid)
                        ids.append(mid)
                if page % 10 == 0:
                    print(f"  page {page}: total unique = {len(seen)}")
                time.sleep(SLEEP_SEC)
                if len(seen) >= TARGET_UNIQUE_MOVIES:
                    return ids
            except requests.RequestException as e:
                print(f"  page {page} error: {e}")
                time.sleep(1.0)
    return ids


ids = fetch_movie_ids()
print(f"\n{len(ids)} unique IDs collected.")
```

## Fetch per-movie details

```{python}
#| label: fetch-details
def fetch_movie_details(movie_ids):
    rows = []
    for i, mid in enumerate(movie_ids, start=1):
        try:
            r = requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/movie/{mid}",
                             params={"api_key": API_KEY, "language": "en-US"},
                             timeout=TIMEOUT)
            if r.status_code != 200:
                continue
            d = r.json()
            rows.append({
                "movie_id": d.get("id"),
                "title": d.get("title"),
                "original_language": d.get("original_language"),
                "release_date": d.get("release_date"),
                "popularity": d.get("popularity"),
                "vote_average": d.get("vote_average"),
                "vote_count": d.get("vote_count"),
                "budget": d.get("budget"),
                "revenue": d.get("revenue"),
                "runtime": d.get("runtime"),
                "status": d.get("status"),
                "adult": d.get("adult"),
                "belongs_to_collection": int(d.get("belongs_to_collection") is not None),
                "genres": json.dumps([g.get("name") for g in (d.get("genres") or [])]),
                "production_countries": json.dumps(
                    [c.get("iso_3166_1") for c in (d.get("production_countries") or [])]),
                "production_companies_n": len(d.get("production_companies") or []),
                "spoken_languages_n": len(d.get("spoken_languages") or []),
                "tagline_len": len(d.get("tagline") or ""),
                "overview_len": len(d.get("overview") or ""),
            })
        except requests.RequestException as e:
            print(f"  detail fetch failed for id={mid}: {e}")
        if i % 50 == 0:
            print(f"  fetched details {i}/{len(movie_ids)}")
        time.sleep(SLEEP_SEC)
    return rows


rows = fetch_movie_details(ids)
df = pd.DataFrame(rows).drop_duplicates(subset=["movie_id"])
out_path = DATA_DIR / "movies_raw.csv"
df.to_csv(out_path, index=False)
print(f"\nSaved {len(df)} rows to {out_path}")
```

## What's in the saved CSV

The columns are: `movie_id`, `title`, `original_language`,
`release_date`, `popularity`, `vote_average`, `vote_count`, `budget`,
`revenue`, `runtime`, `status`, `adult`, `belongs_to_collection`,
`genres` (JSON list), `production_countries` (JSON list),
`production_companies_n`, `spoken_languages_n`, `tagline_len`,
`overview_len`.

`analysis.qmd` reads this CSV directly, so once it is saved you do not
need to re-run this notebook unless you want fresh data.
